title: DART: Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training for Algorithm Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.05988v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recurrent reasoning models (RRMs) can solve structured problems, achieving easy-to-hard generalization through iterative computation in hidden space. These models are typically trained with instance-level supervision, which becomes increasingly problematic as task difficulty grows: valid solutions occupy a tiny region of the solution space, while invalid solutions proliferate rapidly. We propose Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training (DART), a training framework that replaces single-point supervision with a local target distribution around the ground-truth solution and aligns model outputs with this distribution through an adversarial objective. DART provides a richer learning signal and encourages more stable iterative trajectories toward valid solutions. translated_title: DART：面向算法学习的分布式对抗递归训练
translated_abstract: 递归推理模型（RRMs）能够解决结构化问题，通过在隐藏空间中进行迭代计算实现从简单到困难的泛化。这些模型通常采用实例级监督进行训练，但随着任务难度的提升，这种训练方式的问题日益凸显：有效解仅占据解空间的极小区域，而无效解却迅速增多。我们提出了分布式对抗递归训练（DART），该训练框架用真实解周围的局部目标分布取代单点监督，并通过对抗性目标使模型输出与该分布对齐。DART提供了更丰富的学习信号，并促使模型朝着有效解形成更稳定的迭代轨迹。在迷宫（Maze）、国际象棋（Chess）和掩码数独（masked Sudoku）任务上，使用包括深度思维系统和微小递归模型在内的多种递归推理模型进行评估，DART均提升了解题质量、稳定性以及……
tldr: DART通过用真实解周围的局部目标分布替代单点监督，并结合对抗训练目标，显著提升了递归推理模型在迷宫、国际象棋和数独等结构化问题上的求解质量与稳定性。
en_tdlr: DART replaces single-point supervision with a local target distribution around ground-truth solutions via an adversarial objective, improving solution quality and stability of recurrent reasoning models on structured tasks such as Maze, Chess, and Sudoku.
